text: Since Cambodian cattle are mainly draft animals, strong legs/feet matter a great deal for their work capacity. Digital dermatitis: a skin condition usually on the heel bulbs (sometimes between the toes); the classic sign is a standing animal repeatedly flicking a foot for no obvious reason, with reduced working power and lameness — common in cattle that work in mud (e.g. ploughing rice fields), and it can progress into foot rot if untreated, sometimes persisting for months. Treatment: a footbath with 3% formalin (twice daily for 3 days) or 5% copper sulfate, with antibiotics (TMP+Sulfa or Long-Acting Oxytetracycline) added for severe cases; prevention is a soft, dry floor in the shelter. Foot rot: a necrotic (foul-smelling, tissue-destroying) infection between the toes, from wet feces/mud softening the skin there and letting infection enter through injuries (e.g. from sharp stones, metal, wood) — again strongly linked to working in mud. Signs: sudden lameness (usually one foot), fever, a swollen foot, and a break in the skin between the claws with possible pus. Treatment: IV Sulfa 33, TMP+Sulfa for 3 days, or Long-Acting Tetracycline. Arthritis: joint inflammation, usually infection-related. Causes: joint injury (usually affecting one joint); general infections spreading to joints, especially in calves, from the umbilicus, lungs, or gut (Mycoplasma, E. coli, Salmonella); or calcium/phosphorus/trace-mineral deficiency in a milking cow, which in calves causes rickets with deformed forelegs and enlarged carpal joints. Signs: marked lameness, pain on palpating the swollen joint, low appetite, fever. Treatment: antibiotics (Tylosin, Lincomycin, Tetracyclines) for 5–7 days plus pain/inflammation control (Paracetamol, Dipyrone/Analgin/Calmagine). Paralysis/prolonged recumbency: weak, thin cattle unable to stand for many days can develop radial (front leg) paralysis, since unprotected nerves are damaged by lying on one side on a hard surface. Treatment: help the weak animal stand twice daily, inject a stimulant (Carasil, Hematopan B12), and rub the shoulder/thigh with straw.
